Description: Build a reference table that maps each covered SIC code (industry classification) to the list of metrics that should be extracted or calculated from SEC filings for that industry. This table answers the question: for a given SIC, which metrics are required? Format can be JSON, CSV, or a SQL table — store in the existing pipeline repo or database. Each row represents one SIC, with a field listing the applicable metric names (referencing the metric IDs defined in the Metrics Definition Table, DS-002). The table must cover all currently supported SIC codes. Coordinate with DS-002 — both tables should be built together and cross-reference each other.
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] Table created covering all currently supported SIC codes; [ ] Each SIC entry lists the applicable metric names/IDs; [ ] Metric names/IDs match those defined in DS-002 (Metrics Definition Table); [ ] Format is JSON, CSV, or SQL — stored in pipeline repo or database with clear path documented; [ ] Table is readable and usable by the pipeline code without manual transformation; [ ] Reviewed and approved by tech lead before DS-003 begins

Description: Build a comprehensive reference table defining every metric used across all supported SIC codes. Each row represents one metric and must include: metric name (unique slug), display name, description (what the metric measures and why it matters), SEC data source (which filing type: 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K, which financial statement, which specific field or line item), extraction method (direct field extraction vs. calculated — if calculated, include the formula), unit (dollar, percentage, ratio, count, etc.), applicable SIC codes (or all), and notes on edge cases or known data quality issues. Format can be JSON, CSV, or SQL. Coordinate with DS-001.
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] Table covers all metrics currently used across all supported SIC codes; [ ] Every metric row contains: metric_id, metric_name, display_name, description, filing_type, source_statement, source_field, extraction_method (direct/calculated), formula (if calculated), unit, applicable_sics, notes; [ ] Formulas are unambiguous and reproducible; [ ] Source fields reference actual XBRL tags or SEC field names where possible; [ ] Reviewed and approved by tech lead; [ ] Cross-referenced with DS-001 (SIC-to-Metrics mapping)

Summary: [DS] Extend SIC coverage — plan metrics for 10 new SIC codes using LLM
Description: Using the existing 10 SIC codes as reference examples, use an LLM to plan metrics coverage for the next 10 SIC codes identified by the team. For each new SIC: provide the LLM with the industry description, the two reference tables from DS-001 and DS-002, and examples from similar existing SICs. Prompt the LLM to recommend which metrics to extract or calculate, what the SEC data source is, and how to compute each metric. Output a draft extension of both DS-001 and DS-002 tables covering the 10 new SICs. All LLM-generated entries must be flagged as draft pending human review and must not be merged into the production tables until reviewed and approved.
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] 10 new SIC codes confirmed and documented (list approved by team before work begins); [ ] LLM used to draft metric recommendations for each new SIC — prompt template documented and committed to repo; [ ] Draft output covers all 10 new SICs with metric names, SEC sources, and formulas or extraction methods; [ ] Every draft entry flagged as draft pending human review in the table; [ ] Draft tables reviewed by data scientist and at least one domain stakeholder (underwriter or senior analyst); [ ] Approved entries merged into production DS-001 and DS-002 tables; [ ] Rejected or uncertain entries logged with reasoning for future iteration; [ ] Final coverage: 20 SIC codes total across both tables

Summary: [DS] Code migration — move external code to internal OpenShift environment
Description: Migrate the AI generation code developed in the external or local environment into the internal OpenShift environment. This includes all scripts for reading from Azure SQL, assembling prompts, calling the LLM API, parsing responses, and writing output back to Azure SQL. Ensure all dependencies are accounted for (requirements.txt or pyproject.toml), environment variables and secrets are configured using OpenShift Secrets (not hardcoded), and the code runs end-to-end in the internal environment without modification. No functional changes — migration only.
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] All code committed to the internal repo; [ ] requirements.txt or pyproject.toml lists all dependencies with pinned versions; [ ] All secrets (API keys, DB connection strings) read from OpenShift Secrets — not hardcoded anywhere; [ ] Code runs end-to-end in the internal OpenShift environment: reads from Azure SQL, calls LLM API, writes output; [ ] No external network calls to non-approved endpoints; [ ] README updated with internal setup instructions (how to configure secrets, how to run locally against internal env); [ ] Verified by running against at least 3 real companies in the internal environment

Description: Connect to all available internal SecureGPT versions and confirm API connectivity, authentication, and basic response structure for each. Document the version identifiers, base URLs, authentication method (API key format, token endpoint, etc.), and any differences in request or response format between versions. This is a prerequisite for DS-006 (accuracy and consistency evaluation).
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] All available internal SecureGPT versions identified and listed (version name, endpoint URL, model identifier); [ ] Authentication confirmed working for each version from the internal OpenShift environment; [ ] A basic test prompt sent to each version and a valid response received; [ ] Request format differences between versions documented (headers, body structure, model parameter); [ ] Response format differences documented (field names, content structure, token usage fields); [ ] Findings committed to /docs/research/securegpt-versions.md; [ ] Any version that fails connectivity flagged with error details for escalation

Summary: [DS] SecureGPT accuracy, consistency, and token usage evaluation
Description: Run a systematic evaluation of all available internal SecureGPT versions using a standardized test set. Use the same set of 10 companies covering multiple SIC codes as test inputs. For each company, run the Key Insights, Strategic & Risk Insights, and Follow-Up Questions prompts against each SecureGPT version. Measure and record three dimensions: (1) Accuracy — human review of a sample of outputs against source SEC and news data, scored on a defined rubric covering factual grounding, field completeness, and absence of hallucination. (2) Consistency — run each prompt 3 times per company per version, measure variance in output structure and content. (3) Token consumption — input tokens, output tokens, and estimated cost per company per version from the API response. Produce a comparison report with a version recommendation for production use.
Acceptance Criteria: [ ] Test set defined: 10 companies across multiple SIC codes, inputs sourced from Azure SQL; [ ] All three prompt types (Key Insights, Risk Insights, Follow-Up Questions) run against every available SecureGPT version; [ ] Accuracy evaluation: at least 30 output samples reviewed by a human reviewer; accuracy scored on a defined rubric (factual grounding, field completeness, no hallucination); [ ] Consistency evaluation: each prompt run 3 times per company per version; output variance documented (structural differences, content drift, parse failure rate); [ ] Token usage: input_tokens, output_tokens, and estimated cost per company recorded for each version from the API response; [ ] Results compiled into a comparison table: version vs. accuracy score vs. consistency score vs. avg tokens vs. estimated cost per company per batch; [ ] Parse failure rate recorded per version; [ ] Written recommendation produced: which version to use in production and why, with trade-offs noted; [ ] Report reviewed and signed off by tech lead before production version is selected
